paper.title: An Optimal Policy for Dynamic Assortment Planning Under Uncapacitated Multinomial Logit Models

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic assortment planning under uncapacitated MNL model
unmapped: Customer choice follows a multinomial logit (MNL) model with unknown utility parameters v_i >= 0 (v_0 = 1 for no-purchase)
Feedback is the single purchased item (or no purchase) drawn from the MNL choice probabilities
Uncapacitated: any nonempty subset of the N products can be offered
The learner knows the item revenues r_i in [0,1]
Reward is the revenue of the purchased item; expected revenue R(S) = sum r_j v_j / (1 + sum v_j)
settings.definition_quote: At every time time $t$, a retailer picks an assortment $S_t\in \mathbb S$ ($S_t\neq\emptyset$), and observes a purchasing action $i_t\in S_t\cup \{0\}$ ... The distribution of $i_t$ is modeled by the following multinomial-logit (MNL) model ... (A1) $r_\infty := \max_{i\in\mathcal N}r_i \leq 1$.

source.label: thm:upper
source.quote: There exists a universal constant $C_1>0$ such that for all parameters $\{v_i\}_{i=1}^N$ and $\{r_i\}_{i=1}^N$ satisfying $r_i\in[0,1]$, the regret incurred by Algorithm \ref{alg:trisection} satisfies $\reg(\{S_t\}_{t=1}^T) = \mathbb E\sum_{t=1}^TR(S^*)-R(S_t) \leq C_1\sqrt{T\log T}$.

results.notes: Universal constant C_1 unspecified; independent of N.

tuning: Explore with delta = 1/T and adaptive confidence intervals rho_t/t ± sqrt(2 ln(8/(delta t))/t)

source.label: thm:upper-lil
source.quote: There exists a universal constant $C_1>0$ such that for all parameters $\{v_i\}_{i=1}^N$ and $\{r_i\}_{i=1}^N$ satisfying $r_i\in[0,1]$, the regret incurred by the variant of Algorithm \ref{alg:trisection} described above satisfies $\mathrm{Regret}(\{S_t\}_{t=1}^T) =\mathbb E\sum_{t=1}^TR(S^*)-R(S_t) \leq C_1\sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: N-independent; matches lower bound of Theorem 4. Informal Theorem 1 restates Theorems 3 and 4.

conditions: revenue parameters fixed (r_1=1, r_2=1/2, others 0) and known; sup over utilities v_i >= 0

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Let $N$ and $T$ be the number of items and the time horizon that can be arbitrary. There exists revenue parameters $r_1,\cdots,r_N\in[0,1]$ such that for any policy $\pi$, $\sup_{v_1,\cdots,v_N\geq 0} \reg(\{S_t\}_{t=1}^T)  \geq \frac{\sqrt{T}}{384}$.
